text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Eureopean Union external relations commissioner Hans Van den Broek spells out implications on Malta-EU relations of island's decision to freeze EU membership application. Van den Broek told news conference that decision meant the relationship was now between the EU and a third country partner with which the EU wanted close relations. But, he said: "You can't be a member and non-member at the same time, if you see what I mean."
- Corruption commission blames a former minister, now dead, of having acted to prevent a person from being given the go- ahead to build on his property.

- Nationalist Party accuses the government of "not wanting to listen." The opposition party said Prime Minister Alfred Sant left Parliament on Monday as soon as the first opposition speaker rose to speak in debate on new system to replace VAT. As a result, no one else from the opposition spoke on that day.
- General Workers' Union expresses concern over problems for unemployed persons over 50 years old, increasing numbers of whom are having difficulty finding re-employment.
